## Decision analysis · #27971 · 2026-10-30T12:37Z · from os-dev-report 6522980749 (`needs_decision`)

`pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision`. The claim (6522041026) stays; the card thread holds the rider and the docs half on `claude/project-thread-2p9rtc` @ `24787eeb` and opens them as a `Part of #27971` PR now (no behaviour question in either). The main fix waits for the ruling. ⛔ The seat does not answer this.

**One-line problem.** When an operator cancels one item of a batch (a `map` node) and the batch is resumed, the batch finishes as if that item never existed: downstream steps get one result fewer, and every result after the gap sits at the wrong position.

**Background (measured by the dev on `main` `f6adf480`, through `engine.resume`).** A two-item map parks on item 1; `cancelRun(item1)` answers true; `resume(parentId)` advances, the map parks on item 2, and when item 2 completes the parent is `completed` and a downstream node reads `results = [item 2's output]`, `count = 1`. Triage 6516093830 graded the rule: the map may advance, but the item's result records `cancelled`, is never a success, and is readable downstream; a map that cannot record it refuses, as #27877 does.

**Governing text.** `MapConfigSchema.outputVariable` (`packages/spec`): "Each item's subflow output, collected in order." The result is a bare array of outputs, so there is no place for a status. `RESUME_CHILD_PENDING`'s docblock: the item "is still suspended". No ADR decides a cancelled map item (`check-prior-rulings --card 27971`: 13 hits on broad terms, none on this question).

**Protocol.** Every way to record `cancelled` downstream adds an author-readable shape → `Clause-②: yes` for A and B. C changes no shape but widens a refusal code's meaning (one docblock sentence).

| option | what it does | customer-visible result | effort |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A** marker at the item's index | `results[i]` for a cancelled item is a `$`-keyed marker (status `cancelled`, the item run id); `count` = items that ran; spec describe + `flows.mdx` say an element can be that marker | the batch continues; position `i` is still item `i`; a downstream step can see which item was cancelled | M · `packages/spec` describe + service-automation + docs · one PR · contract review owed · no precedent |
| **B** side list | `results` unchanged; the node output gains `cancelled: [{index, runId}]` | the batch continues; `results[i]` silently stops matching item `i` once anything is cancelled | S–M · no spec text (node output undeclared) but a new key |
| **C** refuse | a parent-id resume of a map with a cancelled item answers `409 RESUME_CHILD_PENDING`, naming the cancelled run and telling the operator to cancel the parent | a batch can never continue past a cancelled item; the operator must cancel the whole batch | S · one docblock sentence in `packages/spec` |

**Business reading.** A = a payroll run where one employee's payslip was voided: the run finishes and the register shows that line as "voided". B = the register drops the line and everyone below moves up one row. C = voiding one payslip forces voiding the whole run.

**Named producer (read, not measured — dev's out-of-scope finding).** `plugin-approvals`' revise-window recall calls `cancelRun` on the run parked at the approval. On a batch sign-off (`showcase_release_signoff` → `one_task_signoff`) that run is a map item, so today the batch is left parked and a raw resume is exactly this skip. Under C every such recall strands the batch until the operator cancels it.

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- ① long-term: A grows the contract by one closed marker shape and keeps the ordered-collection invariant; B adds a key and breaks the invariant; C adds nothing but leaves "continue past a cancelled item" impossible.
- ② business pull: real today — any operator cancel on a batch item, and the approval recall path on batch sign-offs (named producer above).
- ③ AI-error: C is the loudest (a refusal with a prescription); A is a closed marker an author can test for; B fails silently (misaligned indexes).
- ④ no-spread: C declares nothing; A declares one marker forever; B declares one key forever.
Prior rulings read: map,cancelled,resume_child_pending,outputvariable → 13 hits; none on a cancelled map item (ADR hits are broad-term: ADR-0014 §4, ADR-0019 D4, ADR-0020 D1/D2, ADR-0032 §3, ADR-0062 D7, ADR-0065 §2, ADR-0080 §2, ADR-0081 §4, ADR-0099 D2); thread: none

**Recommendation: A** (from ① only). In two years a batch step should report per-item status, with cancelled items continuing in place — the shape mainstream orchestrators use (AWS Step Functions' Map reports per-item results/failures with the item identity; Power Automate's apply-to-each keeps iterating and marks the failed iteration). It is also the per-item status record the deferred concurrent fan-out (ADR-0037) needs. B is not taken: it breaks `results[i] = item i` silently. C is not taken: it makes the approval recall strand every batch sign-off. Confidence gap: the marker's exact keys are the dev's proposal and get fixed in the contract review; the approval-recall path is read, not measured.
Self-check: on ① alone, A. Do ②③④ flip it? No — ③④ favour C, but they only argue for keeping the marker closed and small, not for a different letter.

**After the ruling.** A: the seat re-grades the claim to `Clause-②: yes`, adds `packages/spec` (`MapConfigSchema.outputVariable` describe) and `content/docs` (`flows.mdx` batch paragraph) to the surface, the card thread builds it, fable contract review on the final head, then the seat lands. C: the card thread adds the refusal and the docblock sentence, S, no contract review beyond the code-meaning sentence. Either way the rider/docs PR lands first.

Ruling: batch #431 item 3 · letter A · maintainer 「27971 同意」 2026-10-30T13:20Z

Director seat, summon #54 continuation 2 (ledger objectstack#12708, opening mark 6523423511, brief 6523502465). The maintainer answered in the summon chat, verbatim: 「27971 同意」 — the seat's letter **A**.

**What the ruling binds (letter A):** when a `map` item's run was cancelled and the parent is resumed, the map advances and the cancelled item keeps its slot: `results[i]` / `outputVariable[i]` holds a closed, `$`-keyed marker naming status `cancelled` and the item run id (a child flow's output keys never start with `$`, so the marker cannot collide); `count` = items that ran; a cancelled item is never counted as a run or a success; downstream nodes read the marker where they read results. The `MapConfigSchema.outputVariable` describe text and the `flows.mdx` batch paragraph say an element can be that marker. A map that cannot record it refuses, as #27877 does. Not taken: B (a side list; `results[i]` silently stops matching item `i`), C (refuse; the approval recall path strands every batch sign-off). The marker's exact keys are the dev's proposal and are fixed in the contract review, not here.

Governing text: triage 6516093830 (graded rule: advance, record `cancelled`, readable downstream, never a success); `MapConfigSchema.outputVariable` (builtin-node-config.zod.ts L1490); 6513867475 (#27877). Premises re-read at `origin/main` `59547058` (brief 6523502465).

**Workload of the letter:** `domain:server` · the open claim 6522041026 re-graded to `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with `packages/spec` (`MapConfigSchema.outputVariable` describe) and `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` added to the surface · M · contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the final head · `Metadata-protocol: added` (a readable output shape; the seat confirms the arm from the diff) · the rider / docs half already on `claude/project-thread-2p9rtc` lands first as `Part of #27971`.

**Execution:** `needs-user-decision` → `pm:dispatched` in this act (claim 6522041026 by `os-elon-musk` and the card thread stand); server seat 1 re-grades the claim with `Ruling-ref:` naming this comment and the thread builds the main fix.
